extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and KIPO examiners dealing with requests for expedited examination
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evidentiary/claim correspondence requirements for requesting and determining expedited examination (including PPH and PCT-PPH) at the Korean Intellectual Property Office, and special-category eligibility (start-ups, component/materials businesses, government‑awarded inventions, electronic commerce, utility models).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parts & materials-specialized business expedited eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed by a parts·materials-specialized business may be accepted as being 'practiced or prepared to be practiced' for expedited examination without submission of the usual evidential documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevancy between the parts·materials-specialized business and the claimed invention shall be determined based on proving documents (business license, etc.) enclosed in the expedited-examination request form and, if necessary, by referring to KIAT information networks. If relevancy cannot be checked/confirmed, the examiner shall propose a supplement. For joint applications where one applicant is a parts·materials-specialized business, the request is accepted provided names match; evidential documents should be the original confirmation or a certified copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government-awarded invention expedited eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application for an invention awarded in an open contest or competition hosted/run by the government or a local government and financially supported by government/local government for commercialization or for filing shall be accepted for expedited examination on the assumption it is being practiced or to be practiced without submission of proving documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of relevance shall be based on the expedited request form and enclosed proving documents (certificate of merit, certificate, confirmation, awardee selection announcement, financial support document, etc.). Examiner may accept the request without documents if it can be proved by other means that all inventions awarded in the contest receive commercialization/patent‑filing benefits. 'Invention' can include creative idea or art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start-up expedited examination criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications financially supported by the government with over 10 million won for technology development/commercialization, or filed by early-stage startups funded by venture capital, cloud funding, angel investors, or accelerators with over 50 million won, shall be accepted for expedited examination without submission of the usual proving documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination is based on the expedited-examination request form and proving documents (e.g., business license proving early-stage startup). Examples of acceptable proving documents: agreements/affirmations/final evaluation confirmations for government funding; investment performance certificates, investment confirmations, investment commitments for VC/angel/accelerator funding. For joint applications where business name differs from applicant, timing and documentary rules follow the parts·materials-specialized business rules (see that section).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic commerce-related application eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications directly related to electronic commerce that promote electronic transactions under Article 2 of the Framework Act on Electronic Commerce are eligible for expedited examination where recognized necessary for promotion of electronic transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified categories include: (i) transaction methods realized over a network (auctions, reverse auctions, advertising, education, etc.), (ii) electronic money/payment technologies (IC card, network-based electronic money, cyber coin, online payment methods using bank transactions or credit cards), (iii) security or verification technology for electronic transactions (blocking access, transaction verification, electronic signature, smart cards), and (iv) other technologies recognized as crucial for promoting electronic transactions (including tech developed by government or government-funded centers). Examiner guidelines require the application to be related to 'electronic transaction' as defined (definitions of 'electronic document' and 'electronic commerce' provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited examination when prior-art search report from foreign office is available
rubrics_metrics.description: When a prior-art search report related to the concerned application is obtained from a foreign patent office or intergovernmental organization, the requester shall submit evidential documents including the prior-art search report, copies of cited prior-art documents, and a detailed comparison between the claimed invention and the cited prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable prior-art search reports: those prepared by a foreign patent office or an intergovernmental organization (e.g., office action citations, PCT international search report, EPO reports), and reports prepared by an external agency at the request of a foreign patent office. A prior-art search report prepared by the requester themselves or by an external agency on their own initiative shall not be recognized; examiners shall order correction if such reports are submitted. Note: prior-art patent documents cited in the report need not be submitted (examiner can obtain them); non‑patent documents cited must be submitted or the examiner can order their submission. The requester must provide a concise but detailed explanation of differences and possible technical effects, specifying cited parts where relevant; examiner may order supplementation if insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who received a positive decision that at least one claim is allowable from an Office of First Filing (OFF) may request expedited examination at KIPO for a corresponding application that includes claims identical to the allowable claims or claims narrowed by restricting or adding limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participating countries are listed and may change; check KIPO homepage. From Jan 1, 2014, requirements were eased: if the earliest priority date of the corresponding application and the concerned KIPO application are the same, the application may be eligible. Specific cases include mutual priority claim situations and national-phase/PCT situations. The PPH allows KIPO to utilize prior art search and examination results from OFF.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH claim allowability and correspondence requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For PPH, claims in the corresponding application must have been decided allowable by the participating patent office, and all claims of the concerned KIPO application must correspond to those allowable claims (substantially identical or narrowed by added limitations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims indicated allowable include those in a written decision to grant or, absent that, claims indicated allowable in the most recent office action or decision to reject. If allowability is not explicitly indicated due to absence of a ground for rejection, the requester should explain the reason in writing. Where claim categories differ, they are not corresponding; mere differences in translation or claim types (independent/dependent) can be deemed substantially the same. Claim correspondence is determined based on a claim correspondence table that the requester must submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH evidential document requirements and translation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester for expedited examination under PPH must submit specified evidential documents: copy of the claims (including the allowable claims), a copy of the examination-related notification from the participating office, copies of prior arts relied upon (non-patent docs must be provided), and an explanation on correspondence between each claim and the allowable claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner can obtain documents via public networks (AIPN, PAIR, PVS online, etc.), submission may be unnecessary. Documents in languages other than Korean or English must be accompanied by translations unless the examiner can obtain Korean/English translations via networks. The written explanation on claim correspondence is mandatory in all cases and should indicate grounds for correspondence (e.g., literal translation, minor translation differences).

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT-PPH eligibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Under PCT-PPH, a KIPO application is eligible where an international search or international preliminary examination on a corresponding international application (performed in a participating country) includes claims meeting requirements for novelty, inventive step, and industrial applicability, and all claims of the concerned KIPO application correspond to those claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible cases include national-phase applications, applications claiming priority based on the corresponding international application, divisional applications, and applications sharing priority. 'Correspond to' includes substantially identical claims and claims further limited by added limitations; mere translation or claim-type differences are acceptable. Claim correspondence is determined by a submitted claim correspondence table and written explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT-PPH evidential documents and handling of international opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesters for PCT-PPH must submit a copy of the claims recognized to meet requirements in the international search/exam, a copy of the written opinion or international preliminary examination report, copies of prior art cited in those documents (non-patent docs must be provided), and an explanation on correspondence between all claims and those recognized in international proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 'opinions on an international application' (Box VIII) indicate ambiguity or unclear claims, the requester must explain that the concerned KIPO claims are not affected—this may include responses to those opinions or amendments addressing irregularities. If such explanations are missing, examiner may order amendments. Documents in languages other than Korean/English require translations unless obtainable via public networks (Patentscope etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules on submission of prior art (patent vs non-patent) for expedited requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent documents cited in foreign examination reports or international opinions generally need not be submitted because examiners can obtain them; non-patent documents cited must be submitted by the requester, else the examiner may order their submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule applies across foreign-search-based requests, PPH, and PCT-PPH. Failure to submit required non-patent documents can lead to an examiner order to submit or corrective action on the expedited-exam request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination / redetermination and amendment effects on expedited status
rubrics_metrics.description: Determinations on expedited examination made under agreements with foreign offices are not notified to requester unless the request is rejected. If, after determination but before examination starts, the applicant amends claims/specification such that claims are not included in prior comparisons or are not substantially identical to claims recognized as allowable/meeting requirements, the examiner may order corrections and re-determine whether to permit expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner may grant a correction order with a period up to one month at their discretion. If an applicant submits explanations comparing all claims (including amended ones) with prior-art or allowable claims, or submits correspondence explanations for claims meeting international requirements, expedited examination shall be conducted without re-determination. Examiners can order supplementation where explanations are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model expedited-examination exclusion for immediate request-after-filing
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility model registration application that was requested for examination upon filing and then requested for expedited examination within two months from the filing date is not eligible for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional evidential documents do not need to be submitted for utility model expedited requests generally, but this specific timing-triggered exclusion applies. (Context: utility model rights last 10 years and often have shorter technology life-cycles; separate basic requirements discussed.)
